title: Levinas and the Face
hookLine: Emmanuel Levinas taught that another person's face calls us to responsibility
carry: in a face, the commandment speaks first
tomorrow: after the darkest years, what new command did one thinker hear?

cards: Friday night at Saba David's new table, Noa finally said it: she might be in New York all summer. Before he said a single word, she saw his face. Proud, and sad, and trying to hide the sad.
She knew what she owed him before he asked for anything. That's the answer to yesterday's question, and the philosopher Emmanuel Levinas built his ethics on it. A face speaks before anyone speaks.

teach.b: Levinas taught that when you truly face another person, their face isn't just a set of features. It's bare, exposed, open to harm. And from that openness comes a command, before any rule or contract.
As he puts it, its first word is: you shall not kill. Not the law as a paragraph, but the Torah's commandment, "Thou shalt not murder," heard in a living face.

For Levinas, that also means more: don't abandon this person, don't leave them alone. That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: for Levinas, ethics doesn't start with a theory. It starts with a face.
He said this responsibility doesn't wait for fairness. I don't get to say I'll care for you once you care for me.
The face asks first, and I'm already answerable. Noa didn't owe Saba a decision. She owed him her attention, her presence, her not looking away.

how: Levinas's writings on the face and responsibility are studied in Jewish thought and philosophy courses, and his Talmudic readings are read in Jewish study.

o: you can read anyone's mood from their face
a stern look that tells you to obey someone
another person's face calls you to care for them

games.q: a week of later voices — tap the pairs.
p: wonder first; a palace in time
builder and seeker; holiness in details
the face says: you shall not kill

s: for Levinas, responsibility begins once you know someone well
the face commands before any knowing, any word, any contract.
Levinas said the face's first word is: you shall not kill
the commandment heard in a living, exposed face.
Levinas taught responsibility is a fair trade: I care if you do
he said it doesn't wait for fairness; the face asks first.

games.q: your roommate's had an awful week but snapped at you twice. you're annoyed. what would Levinas say comes first?
o: her face, tired and exposed, asks something of you before the score is settled.
an apology from her; then you owe her kindness back.
keeping your distance until she's back to normal.
games.why: for Levinas, responsibility doesn't wait for fairness. the face asks first.

practice: Find a photo of someone you love on your phone or wall. Look at their face, slowly: the eyes, the mouth, the small lines. Ask quietly what that face is asking of you this week.

wordCard.voice: The face commands: Emmanuel Levinas's teaching that another person's face, open and exposed, calls us to responsibility before a word is said.

orig.note: Hebrew: face, presence. the word Levinas's Jewish readers hear behind his face.
